item.title: Fabrizio Romano confirmation sets scene for Liverpool, timeline to sign genius player
item.description: Fabrizio Romano confirmation sets scene for Liverpool, timeline to sign genius player Fabrizio Romano has laid out the timeline and now Liverpool know what they've got to do. A truly genius player will be on the market. Liverpool have made a habit of signing the best-possible talents in world football over the last couple of summers. That thinking has seen them spend over nine figures on three different players, having never come particularly close to spending that before. But it's the new strategy. Sign the best players available and then find a way to build a functioning team out of them. While that last bit has been a struggle up to now, there's a lot of faith in Andoni Iraola to figure it all out. It also means that Liverpool will once again look for a big name in 2027. We do expect major signings in midfield and at centre-back but that doesn't mean the attack is completely sorted. In fact, there is room for another big arrival next year, especially after the Reds tried to sell Cody Gakpo at the end of the transfer window. Couple that with a need for some sort of left-footed attacker and we think the chance is there for arguably the most exciting signing of all. Nico Paz up for grabs Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Nico Paz will not move in January. Instead, it's expected that there will be a battle for his signature next summer when Real Madrid have a buyback clause. This is the second buyback clause they've had for Paz. The first was activated last summer, only for Los Blancos to immediately sell him back to Como with an increased one. Como, then, know they can't control his future beyond next summer. They have no intention of changing that and will refuse any January offers on account of his form this season and importance to the team. Paz is quite clearly one of the biggest prospects in football right now. He was outstanding last season and looks improved in this campaign - a genuinely sensational talent who can seemingly do it all. We've written recently about just how good Paz is and just how much of an impact he could have on Liverpool's attack. He's the kind of player that everyone should try to sign. It's exactly the situation that the Reds current strategy calls for, in fact. One in which you sign the best available player and then look to make it work. Paz is exactly that: the best player available. With the caveat that Real Madrid could ultimately look to integrate him. We feel that's a little unlikely given the wealth of attacking midfield options they already boast - it would be difficult to guarantee him a starting XI role from the get go. Liverpool could. And should.

item.title: "It Always Takes Time to Compete Again" - Enzo Maresca Makes Manchester City Silverware Prediction After Pep Guardiola Exit
item.description: "It Always Takes Time to Compete Again" - Enzo Maresca Makes Manchester City Silverware Prediction After Pep Guardiola Exit Enzo Maresca received heavy backing from Hugo Viana and co in the transfer market upon Pep Guardiola's exit. It is exactly four months since the Italian succeeded Pep Guardiola in the north-west and in doing so, signed up for perhaps the hardest job in world football. Guardiola won 20 major trophies across his decade stationed at the Etihad Stadium, including six Premier League titles, three FA Cup triumphs and an unprecedented Treble in 2023 - the first by an English club since Manchester United in 1999. And while Maresca was part of the Treble-winning year - as Guardiola’s assistant - this job produced an incomparable workload in contrast to his previous roles at Leicester City and Chelsea . Maintaining high standards at the club hasn’t been a difficult task for Maresca, and it seems the 46-year-old has brought an invaluable ability to increase squad cohesion and find a togetherness that is very much overlooked. Manchester City went on an eight-game win streak before losing to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League, where back-to-back wins after that defeat preceded a more recent descent again. Last weekend, City were beaten by Aston Villa away from home and although they won in the Carabao Cup against Saturday’s opponents on Wednesday on penalties, Brighton and Hove Albion looked the better side and should have taken something from the game. Speaking ahead of his side’s second meeting with Brighton in four days, Maresca said: “We’re going in the right direction. After so many years, to change the manager, many players, it always takes time to compete again. On whether his Manchester City side are competing at the moment, he added: “I think, at the moment, we are competing, and we changed many players and changed manager. “But the good thing about the club is that I think we are competing in all competitions, and we know that it takes time, but at this moment we continue in the same way.” A positive start to the season under Maresca - but are errors threatening a total collapse? It has been an incredibly encouraging start to the season for Manchester City , particularly in huge early-season tests against the likes of United, Liverpool and PSG. Even in defeat against Luis Enrique’s side, there were a handful of positives to pick from a much-improved second-half performance, alongside obvious and avoidable mishaps that can be worked on in training. Another example of that came against Villa, where Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma both had games to forget after making mistakes that played into their opponent's hands. The latter was dropped for the Carabao Cup win over Brighton, but is likely to return to the starting squad this weekend as part of several changes across the pitch. item.title: Knueppel’s G League Move Signals Hornets Return Is Close
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets finally have a clear sign that Kon Knueppel is ready to play. The team sent the forward to the Greensboro Swarm for a practice session on Thursday. This move means the 21-year-old is getting his legs back under him after missing the first five games. He was injured during offseason work, and fans have been waiting to see him shoot in a real game. The team confirmed the assignment in a post on X, stating, “OFFICIAL: @hornets have assigned forward Kon Knueppel to the @greensboroswarm for today’s practice.” It is a huge step forward for a player who led the league in three-pointers last year. The Path Back From Injury Knueppel missed the entire preseason and the start of this season due to a strained left hamstring. He suffered the injury just over a month ago. Now, he is using the G League to build up his stamina without the pressure of a full NBA game. These assignments are standard for players recovering from soft tissue issues. Basketnews.com wrote on the team’s decision, “This move is part of his rehabilitation process. Assignments to a G League affiliate for practice are commonly used to give recovering players additional on-court work.” The Hornets need his scoring punch badly. Brandon Miller is averaging 25.6 points per game, but he cannot carry the load alone forever. No Date Set Yet The team has not set a specific date for his return. Naz Reid was benched for not meeting standards, and the offense stalled. The team traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, so they need the young talent to step up. If he practices well on Thursday, he could be ready for the Pistons game on Monday.

item.title: ¡MALAGÓN MANDA MENSAJE TRAS LA MALA RACHA EN EL AZTECA!
item.description: ¡MALAGÓN MANDA MENSAJE TRAS LA MALA RACHA EN EL AZTECA! El guardameta del América reconoció que el equipo atraviesa una racha de cinco partidos sin ganar; sin embargo, aseguró que el grupo mantiene la tranquilidad El Club América atraviesa un momento en el que los resultados no han acompañado al equipo como esperaba su afición. Son cinco partidos sin conocer la victoria, una situación que representa un desafío para una institución acostumbrada a competir por los primeros lugares. Sin embargo, dentro del vestidor azulcrema mantienen la confianza en que el panorama puede cambiar. Durante la conferencia de prensa previa al encuentro frente a Toluca, Luis Ángel Malagón habló sobre la actualidad del conjunto americanista y dejó claro que, pese a la racha negativa, el equipo no pierde de vista sus objetivos. “Son cinco partidos de no ganar, pero todo es parte de… al final seguimos en la parte alta y mañana será un rival más”, expresó el arquero azulcrema. CONFIANZA TOTAL EN AMÉRICA Las palabras de Malagón reflejan la postura de un equipo que busca mantener la calma en medio de la exigencia que representa defender los colores del América. El guardameta reconoció implícitamente que los resultados recientes no han sido los esperados, pero también puso sobre la mesa un aspecto importante: el conjunto continúa ubicado en la parte alta de la clasificación. Te recomiendo AMÉRICA DEJA ESCAPAR EL TRIUNFO ANTE XOLOS El compromiso ante Toluca representa una nueva oportunidad para que las Águilas puedan reencontrarse con la victoria y comenzar a dejar atrás esta racha. No será un encuentro sencillo, pues enfrente tendrán a un rival que también llega con aspiraciones importantes dentro del campeonato. Para Malagón, el mensaje es claro: mantener la tranquilidad, trabajar y afrontar cada partido con la responsabilidad que exige representar al americanismo.

item.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
item.description: null India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ). NavIC operates on a smaller scale than its American counterpart, however. It's "a regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) service to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km [930 miles] beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area," ISRO officials wrote in the NVS-03 launch brochure . The Indian constellation currently consists of three fully functioning satellites, and it requires four to provide PNT services. So today's launch was a big deal — and a lot of eyes will be watching NVS-03's commissioning and checkout phase. Today's launch was the 14th to date for the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) Mark II, a three-stage rocket that stands 170 feet (52 meters) tall. Twelve of those 14 liftoffs have been successful. The GSLV Mark II debuted in 2010, the same year its predecessor retired. That previous launchers, the Mark I, flew a total of six times, with two failures. NVS-03 was the fourth Indian launch of 2026 and the third operated by ISRO. The fourth was mounted by Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company ever to successfully reach orbit .

item.title: Chad Kelly’s Historic CFL Deal Proves NFL Wrong
item.description: Nov 9, 2024; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Toronto Argonauts quarterback Chad Kelly (12) passes the ball against the Montreal Alouettes during the first quarter at Percival-Molson Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images His new contract makes Chad Kelly the first million-dollar player in the league’s salary cap era. The NFL passed on him, but the CFL is now paying him like a franchise cornerstone. According to multiple reports, including figures cited by the New York Post , the deal could reach $5,805,250, including bonuses. That is real money for a man the NFL labeled Mr. Irrelevant. The numbers tell the story of a player who found his footing after being discarded. Before this extension, BC Lions quarterback Nathan Rourke held the title of highest-paid player with a salary of $684,700. Kelly’s new deal dwarfs that figure and changes the economic landscape for every quarterback in Canada. He posted career highs this season with 5,067 passing yards and 33 touchdowns. Those stats are not just good; they are elite by any standard. A Home in Toronto Kelly did not just sign a check; he found a place to stay. During a press conference on Tuesday, he said coming to the CFL “was the best decision I ever made in my life.” He added that he has a beautiful family and has “come to love Canada on a whole other level.” He stated that he “never knew I could come to love a place so much (more) than my home and now this is my home forever,” and that he is “just thankful to be in this situation.” This sentiment matters because it shows he is not just passing through. He helped the Argonauts win the Grey Cup in 2022 and has been a key part of their offense since. The NFL treated him as a bust after taking him last overall in the 2017 draft. He never found his footing there. Now he is the face of the league in Canada with a contract that secures his future. The Cost of Being Mr. Irrelevant The NFL draft is a cruel machine that often throws away talent . Kelly was the last pick in 2017. He is the nephew of Buffalo Bills great Jim Kelly, which makes the NFL’s rejection even more striking. He spent years bouncing around before finding success in the CFL. The league that ignored him is now watching from the sidelines while he signs a historic extension. Although the Argonauts did not release financial terms after the official announcement, the reported figures are clear. This deal proves that a player can rebuild a career if given the chance. Kelly set new records this year, and the team rewarded him accordingly. The gap between his NFL draft status and his current value is massive. He is no longer a question mark. He is the highest-paid player in the league and a proven winner. The NFL missed out on a quarterback who can throw for over 5,000 yards and lead a team to a championship. That is a mistake the league will have to live with. Kelly is settled in Toronto and ready to play for years to come.

item.title: Cyberbullying : Okafor’s lawyer faults Sowore, others over sentimental support for Ogala
item.description: By Henry Ojelu Counsel to Pastor Chris Okafor, Mr Ife Ajayi, has faulted the sentimental support for Nollywood actress Doris Ogala over her cyberbullying trial, insisting that freedom of expression does not confer the right to make false and malicious allegations against others without regard for the law. Ajayi, who spoke in an interview with Vanguard, was reacting to comments by activist Omoyele Sowore and Ogala over alleged injustice in the ongoing trial. He argued that the right to freedom of expression was not absolute and must be exercised within the limits prescribed by law, particularly where allegations, blackmail and extortion were involved. According to him, the issues leading to the criminal proceedings should not be treated as a mere disagreement between individuals, but viewed against the background of alleged violations of the rights of others. Ajayi advised the public to obtain copies of the charges proffered against her. He described her unlawful conduct as a deliberate act that violated the rights of his client and was capable of inciting the public against an individual. He also urged members of the public to exercise caution in endorsing false allegations made by the actress, insisting that such claims should be subjected to legal scrutiny rather than public sentiment. Expressing confidence in the judiciary, the lawyer said he was optimistic that the court would deliver justice based on the overwhelming print, audio and video evidence in compliance with the applicable laws. “I am 100 per cent optimistic that the court will do what is right. The court, in all fairness, even after the defendant’s lawyer pleaded with it to release her on bail and offered to take responsibility for her conduct, gave the prosecution 48 hours to respond,” he said. Ajayi also faulted Ogala’s conduct during the court proceedings, alleging that her outburst and disruption of proceedings raised questions about her ability to abide by the conditions of her release. He said the incident suggested that even her counsel might have difficulty guaranteeing her conduct if she were granted bail. The lawyer maintained that the courtroom was not a place for emotional outbursts or disrespect, stressing that parties to a legal proceeding were expected to conduct themselves in accordance with established rules. “You cannot behave disrespectfully at a police station or anywhere else and expect to do the same in a court of law. The court is where logic and legal accountability prevail,” he said. Ajayi further called on the National Assembly to consider stricter legislation against the practice of publicly calling out individuals over private disagreements, particularly where such actions could damage reputations or violate the rights of others. He argued that personal grievances should be addressed through appropriate legal channels rather than through public accusations and campaigns. “The law is not about emotion or sentiment. item.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
item.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable . With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). It will live within a website's robots.txt file , which has long signaled which web crawlers can and can't scrape a site - whether for search indexing, archiving, or … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: ‎NSITF seeks stronger enforcement of Employees’ Compensation Act to protect workers’ rights
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — MANAGING Director and Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Mr. Oluwaseun Faleye, has urged the judiciary to strengthen the interpretation, adjudication, and enforcement of the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA) 2010, so that Nigerian workers can fully enjoy the justice and protection the law guarantees. ‎ ‎The Act provides compensation for employees—or their dependants—who suffer death, injury, disability, or occupational disease arising from employment. ‎ ‎Faleye, in his welcome address at the opening of the NSITF 2026 Legal Stakeholders’ Engagement in Abuja, ‎emphasised that legislation alone is not enough; workers need timely dispute resolution, fair hearings, and effective compliance with court orders to turn statutory rights into real benefits. ‎The theme of the two-day event is “Enhancing Judicial Interpretation, Adjudication and Enforcement under the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA), 2010.” ‎ ‎Mr. Faleye noted that while last year’s engagement focused on strengthening collaboration for the sustainable administration of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme, this year’s edition addresses a deeper question: how statutory rights can be translated into practical justice. ‎ ‎Drawing on the experience of everyday Nigerian workers — mothers, construction workers, factory employees and drivers who leave home each day expecting to return he observed that a workplace accident instantly becomes a human crisis with financial, emotional and social consequences. ‎ ‎”Does the law provide a framework for protection? Yes. Does the Employees’ Compensation Act establish a system for compensation for work-related injury, disease, disability or death? Yes. But the existence of a law does not by itself guarantee that its promise will be fulfilled,” Mr. Faleye said. ‎ ‎He explained that the effectiveness of the ECA depends on three interconnected stages — interpretation, adjudication and enforcement: ‎”First, are the provisions being understood and applied in a manner consistent with their wording, purpose and legal context? ‎ ‎”Second, are disputes being resolved fairly, on evidence and applicable law, without avoidable delay? Third, are lawful decisions and orders being given effect so that justice does not end with the pronouncement of judgment? Weakness at any stage can undermine confidence in the entire system.” ‎ ‎The NSITF Managing Director underscored the pivotal role of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN) in labour justice, noting that the Court’s interpretation of the Employees’ Compensation Act has consequences beyond the immediate parties to a dispute. ‎ ‎Such decisions, he said, clarify rights, guide the conduct of employers and employees, and shape the resolution of future disputes. ‎ ‎For workers, he said, justice means the practical realisation of their entitlements; for employers, it means a predictable legal environment. Yes. Does the Employees’ Compensation Act establish a system for compensation for work-related injury, disease, disability or death? Yes. But the existence of a law does not by itself guarantee that its promise will be fulfilled,” Mr. Faleye said. ‎ ‎He explained that the effectiveness of the ECA depends on three interconnected stages — interpretation, adjudication and enforcement: ‎”First, are the provisions being understood and applied in a manner consistent with their wording, purpose and legal context? ‎ ‎”Second, are disputes being resolved fairly, on evidence and applicable law, without avoidable delay? Third, are lawful decisions and orders being given effect so that justice does not end with the pronouncement of judgment? Weakness at any stage can undermine confidence in the entire system.” ‎ ‎The NSITF Managing Director underscored the pivotal role of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN) in labour justice, noting that the Court’s interpretation of the Employees’ Compensation Act has consequences beyond the immediate parties to a dispute. ‎ ‎Such decisions, he said, clarify rights, guide the conduct of employers and employees, and shape the resolution of future disputes. ‎ ‎For workers, he said, justice means the practical realisation of their entitlements; for employers, it means a predictable legal environment. The credibility of the Scheme, he added, rests on workers’ confidence that legitimate claims will be addressed and on employers’ confidence that their obligations will be determined fairly. ‎ ‎Mr. Faleye, a legal practitioner, affirmed that the Fund will continue to strengthen its administrative processes, improve claims handling, promote awareness and encourage employer compliance. He acknowledged, however, that the NSITF cannot achieve these objectives in isolation. ‎ ‎He urged participants to treat the engagement not as a ceremonial gathering, but as an opportunity to identify practical solutions, highlight areas requiring greater legal clarity, improve cooperation, reduce avoidable disputes and promote compliance. ‎ ‎”The value of a stakeholder engagement lies not merely in the quality of speeches delivered but in the clarity of understanding it produces and the improvements that follow,” he said, calling for frank, informed and constructive deliberations that will yield actionable recommendations for strengthening the administration of the Scheme. ‎ ‎”May our deliberations strengthen the rule of law and ensure that the promise of protection becomes a reality for Nigerian workers,” he added. ‎ ‎In his goodwill message, the Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi, stated that the strength of a nation lies not merely in the laws it makes, but in the wisdom with which those laws are applied and the integrity of the institutions entrusted with their administration. ‎ ‎While laws may establish rights and define obligations, the Minister said, public confidence ultimately rests on the assurance that justice will be administered fairly, impartially and with due regard for the dignity of every individual. ‎ ‎Recalling the enduring words of the late Justice Chukwudifu Oputa that “the judiciary is the last hope of the common man,” the Minister observed that “…this statement carries a profound responsibility. ‎ ‎It reminds us that for many citizens, the justice system represents their final recourse when other avenues have failed. Such trust must never be taken lightly.” Such trust, he said, demands wisdom in judgment, integrity in public service and an unwavering commitment to fairness. ‎ ‎The Minister reaffirmed the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment’s belief that a just and productive society must be built on respect for the law, responsible institutions and a shared commitment to the public good, and urged all stakeholders in the administration of the ECA to approach their responsibilities with these values in mind. ‎ ‎”The credibility of our institutions is strengthened not by words alone, but by the quality and integrity of their actions,” he stressed. ‎ ‎He commended the NSITF Management under Mr. Faleye for convening the engagement, describing it as an important national initiative aimed at strengthening the implementation of the ECA 2010. ‎ ‎ He also expressed appreciation to the President of the National Industrial Court, distinguished members of the Bench and Bar, and all participants for their commitment. ‎ ‎”May your deliberations be guided by wisdom, enriched by experience and directed towards outcomes that strengthen public confidence in our institutions,” the Minister said. ‎ ‎Delivering the keynote address, the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Benedict Bakwaph Kanyip, advocated institutional synergy to strengthen the Employees’ Compensation Scheme and ensure that its benefits reach the intended beneficiaries. ‎ ‎He commended the NSITF for creating a platform that will enhance the Scheme in the overall interest of Nigerians and the workplace, adding that robust engagement with the judiciary will further boost the Fund’s impact on service delivery under the Scheme. ‎ ‎The event drew senior government and judicial officials, including the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria; the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Honourable Justices of the National Industrial Court; members of the Bench and Bar; Employers’ Associations; organised labour; and development partners. The post ‎NSITF seeks stronger enforcement of Employees’ Compensation Act to protect workers’ rights appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ₦70,000 transport allowance: Federal pensioners decry exclusion, unpaid ₦25,000 palliative
item.description: — Beg Tinubu to intervene By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — CONTROVERSY over the recent approval of ₦70,000 for Federal Government workers has continued unabated, as the Federal Parastatals and Private Sector Pensioners Association of Nigeria (FEPPPAN) has appealed to President Bola Tinubu to extend the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants to pensioners. The retired government workers lamented that retirees were being left behind in government efforts to cushion the effects of rising living costs. FEPPPAN said pensioners also pay transportation fares to hospitals for medical care, markets to purchase essential commodities, and other destinations for economic activities they undertake to supplement their pensions and sustain their livelihoods. In a statement jointly signed by its President-General, Elder Benjamin Maisamari Amako, and General Secretary, Mr Franklin Erinle, the association questioned why retirees should be excluded from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising fares and other costs of living. According to the statement: “The association questioned the rationale behind excluding pensioners from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising transport fares and other costs of living. “FEPPPAN expressed further disappointment over the continued non-payment of the ₦25,000 monthly subsidy-removal palliative announced by the Federal Government in October 2023, lamenting that eligible pensioners were still awaiting the promised relief even as another support package had been approved for serving workers.” It called for immediate presidential intervention to address the concerns of pensioners. The statement said: “FEPPPAN expresses concern that eligible pensioners are yet to receive the promised support, describing the continued wait as a source of frustration for retirees who had hoped that the intervention would provide some relief from the prevailing economic hardship. “Against this background, the association called on President Tinubu to urgently intervene by directing the relevant government agencies to ensure the payment of the outstanding ₦25,000 subsidy-removal palliative to eligible pensioners. “It also urged the President to ensure that pensioners are included in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement, stressing that retirees should not be left out of policies intended to protect Nigerians from the effects of rising living costs.” It clarified that its appeal was not against the transport allowance approved for serving workers, but against the apparent neglect of retirees in the government’s response to the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It lamented that pensioners, many of whom depend on fixed monthly incomes to pay for food, medication, transportation and other necessities, were being left to contend with rising expenses without comparable relief. FEPPPAN recalled that on October 1, 2023, the Federal Government announced a ₦25,000 monthly palliative for three months to cushion the effects of petrol subsidy removal, with vulnerable pensioners among the groups identified for assistance. It said the continued wait for the promised relief had deepened retirees’ frustration and hardship. The association urged Tinubu to direct the relevant government agencies to expedite the payment of the outstanding palliative to eligible pensioners and ensure their inclusion in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement. FEPPPAN maintained that pensioners deserved the same consideration in government policies intended to ease economic hardship, stressing that their years of service to the country should not leave them forgotten when relief measures are being implemented. item.title: IGP secures Italian training offer for 5,000 police officers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has secured an offer of specialised training for up to 5,000 Nigeria Police Force personnel in Italy as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s response to terrorism and other security threats. The proposed training, focusing on counter-insurgency operations and policing in difficult rural and forested terrains, followed Disu’s working visit to Italy, where he held discussions with Italian law enforcement authorities on security cooperation, technology transfer and institutional development. The initiative is aimed at enhancing the operational capacity of the police to tackle terrorism, kidnapping, arms trafficking and other criminal activities through intelligence-led policing and improved tactical capabilities. A statement issued on Friday by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the proposed training would cover tactical operations, intelligence-led patrols, protection of critical infrastructure, digital and scientific forensics, cybercrime, explosives detection, financial investigations, asset tracing and anti-extortion techniques. It said the programme would extend beyond the Police Mobile Force to include specialised units such as explosive ordnance disposal and forensic teams. During the visit, Disu met with the Commander General of the Italian Carabinieri, Lieutenant-General Salvatore Luongo, to explore opportunities for technical assistance, specialised training and institutional cooperation. The IGP and his delegation also visited the Carabinieri Centre of Excellence for Stability Police Units (CoESPU) in Vicenza, where they assessed training facilities and explored ways of adapting specialised programmes to Nigeria’s security challenges. Among the proposals discussed were command courses for 40 senior police officers, leadership training for 100 junior commanders and the deployment of a mobile assistance team to support Police Mobile Force training schools in Gwoza and Ila-Orangun. The delegation also sought Italian support for developing a national stability policing doctrine and standard operating procedures to promote professionalism, operational consistency and civilian protection, particularly in communities recovering from conflict. Further discussions focused on possible cooperation in canine operations, forensic science and mounted policing, including horse breeding and local capacity development for public order management and other policing responsibilities. To facilitate the implementation of the proposed initiatives, Disu proposed a memorandum of understanding covering training, technology transfer and operational doctrine. He also invited an assessment team from the Italian Carabinieri to Abuja to identify priority areas and develop practical implementation strategies. item.title: All Esper locations in Final Fantasy Resonance
item.description: Final Fantasy Resonance 's Espers give Fina an extra edge in combat, or sometimes they're just convenient decoys to bait the enemy into attacking them and not your party. However you use them, Espers are definitely worth the MP it costs to summon them. You have to put in some extra work to obtain them, though. Espers are tucked away in different spots around Resonance 's world, and you have to find and often fight them before Fina can use their powers.

item.title: ‘Debt Worse Than Leprosy’: Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said. He urged Nigerian leaders to scrutinise foreign economic prescriptions and ensure that national policies reflected the country’s interests and development priorities. Turning to artificial intelligence, Obasanjo warned that Africa risked repeating the mistakes of its colonial past if it allowed foreign interests to control the technology and its applications. Although he acknowledged that he was not technically knowledgeable about AI, he said ownership and control were critical to ensuring that the technology served African interests. “I don’t know too much technically about AI, but I know that anything that is not under your control can be abused against you. And you can see that this has already started,” he said. Drawing parallels between AI and Africa’s historical experiences with slavery, colonialism and economic dependency, Obasanjo urged African leaders to approach the technological revolution with caution. He also questioned the concept of technology transfer, asking African countries to examine the terms and benefits of their engagements with foreign technology providers. “But what exactly is technology transfer? Who transferred technology to them, and what did they pay for it?” he queried. Obasanjo further criticised what he described as unequal international economic arrangements, citing restrictions on agricultural subsidies for developing countries despite continued support for farmers in developed economies. He expressed concern over the estimated 24 million Nigerian children out of school, warning that the situation could create serious challenges for future generations. “We have 24 million Nigerian children who should be in school but are not. If you are looking for the disasters of tomorrow, these children represent one of them,” he said. He challenged policymakers and technology stakeholders to explore how AI could improve access to education and address learning challenges. On agriculture, Obasanjo advocated the deployment of artificial intelligence to help farmers identify suitable crops, improve productivity and strengthen food and nutrition security. Also speaking at the event, guest speaker and historian, Dr Umar Ardo, warned that Africa could be entering another phase of economic exploitation through artificial intelligence if it failed to secure ownership and control of its data, technological infrastructure and intellectual resources. In a presentation titled, “From Slave Ships to Server Farms: Artificial Intelligence and Africa’s Unbroken History of Extraction”, Ardo argued that although AI offered significant opportunities for economic transformation, it could deepen existing inequalities if African countries remained dependent on foreign technology companies. He said the continent must move beyond adopting foreign innovations and address fundamental questions surrounding ownership, control, regulation and the distribution of economic benefits. “AI offers Africa important opportunities, but without ownership, safeguards and public purpose, it could extend a long history in which Africa supplies value while others control and capture it,” he said. Tracing Africa’s economic history over five centuries, Ardo identified the transatlantic slave trade, colonial exploitation of natural resources and post-independence economic dependency as major phases of external extraction. He explained that while the slave trade commodified African lives, colonialism focused largely on exploiting mineral and agricultural resources, while many post-independence economies remained dependent on exporting raw materials and importing finished products. According to him, infrastructure and technologies introduced during colonial rule, including railways, steam engines and administrative systems, were largely organised around extracting African resources and transporting them to foreign markets. “We supplied resources and labour; others controlled the machinery and captured much of the value,” he stated. Ardo also identified the migration of highly trained African professionals, including doctors, nurses, engineers and scientists, to foreign countries as another dimension of the continent’s continuing resource losses. He warned that data could become the next major commodity in Africa’s history of external extraction, noting that information generated by citizens, hospitals, farmers, businesses, indigenous communities and public institutions was increasingly valuable to the global digital economy. “Data may become the fourth commodity in this long history of extraction,” he cautioned. The historian expressed concern that the infrastructure for processing information, developing AI models and generating intellectual property and commercial profits remained disproportionately controlled outside Africa. item.title: Emery’s focus fully on Fulham despite Barcelona tie
item.description: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has said Fulham will have his complete attention on Saturday despite next week’s high-profile Champions League tie away to Barcelona. Villa will be bidding for their third successive win in the Premier League against the Cottagers before taking on Spanish champions Barcelona in Europe. “If I am thinking, if we are thinking, after the match tomorrow against Fulham, we are making a mistake, and we are wrong, completely wrong,” Emery told reporters on Friday ahead of the match at Villa Park. “So, tomorrow, Fulham, prioritising Premier League clearly, and this is the message,” said the Spaniard, whose side ended leaders Manchester City’s perfect start to the season with a 2-1 win last week. “To keep our consistency, to keep our demands and work every day. To get this commitment to keep our consistency like we did last year. Each match is a test. “In the Premier League, we lack points. Of course, we are progressing, we are getting better. But, if we want to be consistent like last year and in the top positions, we must focus on tomorrow’s match, prioritising 100 percent and focusing, respecting them (Fulham).” Birmingham club Villa are currently ninth in the Premier League table, three points ahead of London side Fulham. item.title: Zamfara shows transformational leadership under Lawal — EFCC chairman
item.description: The Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr Ola Olukoyede, has described developments in Zamfara State under Governor Dauda Lawal as evidence of transformational leadership. Olukoyede spoke on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the 30th anniversary lecture of Zamfara State, held at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau. He said he accepted the invitation to speak at the event after conducting personal checks on the governor and the state’s development trajectory, particularly over the past three years. The EFCC chairman explained that his office’s ethical demands generally kept him away from political events and government houses, but that what he discovered about Zamfara persuaded him to attend. “By virtue of the ethical demands of my office, I don’t attend political events; I don’t go to the government house as a matter of principle. But when I received this invitation, something told me to accept and see what was going on there,” he said. Olukoyede said he had also discussed his findings with President Bola Tinubu, who encouraged him to attend the anniversary celebration. He said his arrival in Gusau offered him an opportunity to observe some of the infrastructure projects and changes taking place in the state. “As I arrived in Gusau, the first thing I noticed was the new airport. It is noticeable even to first-time visitors. The capital city speaks of visible transformation, as we have seen. Newly paved roads align with street solar lights,” he said. According to him, Zamfara had for years remained among Nigeria’s less-developed states despite its natural potential and efforts by successive administrations. He, however, said the state’s outlook was changing, adding that the physical development of Gusau reflected broader changes across Zamfara. The EFCC chairman also commended the state government’s reported progress in education, particularly its performance in national examinations conducted by the National Examinations Council (NECO) and the West African Examinations Council (WAEC). He attributed the developments to what he described as deliberate reform initiatives by the Lawal administration, noting that they aligned with the anniversary lecture’s theme, “Accountability and Responsibility in Transformational Government”. Olukoyede said the decision to invite the EFCC chairman to address the state anniversary reflected the governor’s commitment to transparency and accountability. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the anniversary theme, “Reflections, Achievements, and the Future”, was designed to provide an opportunity to examine the challenges that had shaped the state’s journey and consider the responsibilities of leaders in securing a better future. He said the anniversary lecture had provided a platform for intellectual engagement on critical issues, including public accountability, community participation in tackling insecurity, preservation of history and culture, and the relat

In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the anniversary theme, “Reflections, Achievements, and the Future”, was designed to provide an opportunity to examine the challenges that had shaped the state’s journey and consider the responsibilities of leaders in securing a better future. He said the anniversary lecture had provided a platform for intellectual engagement on critical issues, including public accountability, community participation in tackling insecurity, preservation of history and culture, and the relationship between security and socio-economic development. Lawal said the discussions were central to his administration’s development agenda, particularly its Six-Point Rescue Agenda and the Zamfara State Development Plan 2025–2034. According to him, the development plan provides a long-term framework for the state’s economic growth, infrastructure, social welfare, human capital development, governance and environmental sustainability. “We must turn these commitments into measurable improvements in people’s lives,” the governor said. He expressed appreciation to the speakers, discussants, organising committee and other participants for their contributions to the anniversary programme. Other speakers at the anniversary lecture included Professors Tijjani Muhammad Bande, Sulaiman Kura, Murtala Rufai and Taofik Aminu. item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira today appreciated to N1,373 per dollar from N1,380 in the parallel market on Thursday. But the naira was stable at N1,346 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N27 per dollar from N36 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 8.9 per cent to $58.9 billion from $54.05 billion on Thursday. Analysts expect the mixed performance of the naira in the following weeks. In their financial market review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management Limited said, “Going forward, we expect the naira to remain relatively mixed across the foreign exchange markets in the near term, supported by marginal improvements in external reserves and potential foreign exchange inflows. “However, sustained pressure on foreign currency demand could limit further gains.” The post Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NASA Releases MAX POWER Key Events for Media, Participants

Credit: NASA/Jordan Cochran AmAmerica’s newest aerospace expo and air show – MAX POWER – is fast approaching, and NASA has announced key events beginning Friday, Nov. 6, and running through Sunday, Nov. 8, hosted on and near the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Through multiple park experiences at MAX POWER , NASA and a variety of external collaborators will showcase the newest aircraft, autonomous vehicles, technologies, and more defining the future of air and space. NASA will display its quiet supersonic X-59 plane, and agency partners will showcase Moon rovers, spacecraft, and more. The expo also is a culmination of the agency’s recent Inspiration Tour , which included numerous flyovers to highlight NASA’s fleet of aircraft. A current schedule of events is available on the agency’s website . MAX POWER includes opportunities to meet leadership, astronauts, engineers, scientists, and other subject matter experts during the family-friendly public events with gates opening at 9 a.m. EST on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8. NASA also will share multiple news updates during the weekend, including hosting a news conference at 5 p.m. on Nov. 7, to provide its latest Moon Base update. Located near the lunar South Pole, the Moon Base is humanity’s first outpost for long-term lunar exploration. Live coverage of the news conference will stream on a variety of platforms online. item.title: US midterm early voting hits record 48 million
item.description: A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Friday. The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022. The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency. In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running around 50 percent ahead of the same stage in 2022. North Carolina’s election board reported early voting up nearly 37 percent on the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go. In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running around two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state’s office. In states that record voters’ party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans. Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up around 44 percent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 percent for Republicans and 25 percent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters. University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border. In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state’s midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 percent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 percent for men. “Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system,” top elections official Brad Raffensperger said Thursday. But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome. A voter’s party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday. In recent elections Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats’ early advantage. And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting ballots sooner than in previous elections. The post US midterm early voting hits record 48 million appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
item.description: null In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1. Jason X (2001) (Image credit: New Line Cinema / Crystal Lake Entertainment) 2001 was a really weird time for the Friday the 13th franchise. New Line had acquired the series in the wake of the terrible box office returns and critical panning of Friday the 13th Part VIII: Jason Takes Manhattan. Known as "the house that Freddy built," New Line's plan was clear: pit Voorhees vs. Kruger in a battle of horror icons for the ages. However, the studio had to keep Jason in the public eye to ensure the eventual crossover lived up to expectations. The first move in that effort, 1993's Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday, was an odd start. The movie apparently kills Voorhees, with his iconic hockey mask seized by the equally iconic bladed glove of Freddy Krueger at the end of the film and dragged into the dirt. Fun bit of trivia: the hand wearing the glove isn't that of Freddy actor Robert Englund but belongs to Kane Hodder, arguably the best Jason Voorhees, meaning Hodder played both Jason and Freddy! Still, the crossover has stalled in the preproduction process by 2001, as a script couldn't be agreed upon. New Line wanted a new Friday film but in a different environment than the typical Crystal Lake setting. After rejecting a winter-themed movie that would see Voorhees killing cross-country skiers in a snow-covered Camp Crystal Lake, New Line decided to put Jason on ice in a different way, cryogenically freezing Pamela Voorhees' baby boy and sending him to space in Jason X, the tenth movie in the series. Jason X would see the Crystal Lake Killer slaughter David Croenberg, get his ass kicked by a feisty robot, and double up on his iconic sleeping bag kill from Friday the 13th Part VII: The New Blood (one of my favorites, massively underrated), all on the way to getting a major upgrade from some very unhelpful nanobots to become Uber Jason. Jason X has a mixed reputation and isn't regarded as one of the better entries in the series, but the movie has a load of positives going for it. The kills are super inventive, the nitrogen head smash being arguably one of the best in a series known for over-the-top brutality; Kane Hodder is great during his final shift as Jason, and there are a load of laughs. Jason X isn't as tongue-in-cheek as one
item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1. Jason X (2001) (Image credit: New Line Cinema / Crystal Lake Entertainment) 2001 was a really weird time for the Friday the 13th franchise. New Line had acquired the series in the wake of the terrible box office returns and critical panning of Friday the 13th Part VIII: Jason Takes Manhattan. Known as "the house that Freddy built," New Line's plan was clear: pit Voorhees vs. Kruger in a battle of horror icons for the ages. However, the studio had to keep Jason in the public eye to ensure the eventual crossover lived up to expectations. The first move in that effort, 1993's Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday, was an odd start. The movie apparently kills Voorhees, with his iconic hockey mask seized by the equally iconic bladed glove of Freddy Krueger at the end of the film and dragged into the dirt. Fun bit of trivia: the hand wearing the glove isn't that of Freddy actor Robert Englund but belongs to Kane Hodder, arguably the best Jason Voorhees, meaning Hodder played both Jason and Freddy! Still, the crossover has stalled in the preproduction process by 2001, as a script couldn't be agreed upon. New Line wanted a new Friday film but in a different environment than the typical Crystal Lake setting. After rejecting a winter-themed movie that would see Voorhees killing cross-country skiers in a snow-covered Camp Crystal Lake, New Line decided to put Jason on ice in a different way, cryogenically freezing Pamela Voorhees' baby boy and sending him to space in Jason X, the tenth movie in the series. Jason X would see the Crystal Lake Killer slaughter David Croenberg, get his ass kicked by a feisty robot, and double up on his iconic sleeping bag kill from Friday the 13th Part VII: The New Blood (one of my favorites, massively underrated), all on the way to getting a major upgrade from some very unhelpful nanobots to become Uber Jason. Jason X has a mixed reputation and isn't regarded as one of the better entries in the series, but the movie has a load of positives going for it. The kills are super inventive, the nitrogen head smash being arguably one of the best in a series known for over-the-top brutality; Kane Hodder is great during his final shift as Jason, and there are a load of laughs. Jason X isn't as tongue-in-cheek as one of the following movies on this list, but it is definitely self-aware and so much better for it. In honor of arguably the best of these space-relocated horror movies, we'll rate this and the following movies in Uber Jasons out of five. For campy space-based horror featuring a character that is a fish out of water, Jason X is near perfect. 4.8 Uber Jasons out of 5. Hail to the king, baby. 2. Amityville in Space (2022) (Image credit: Polonia Brothers Entertainment) Alien is often referred to as "a haunted house movie in space." The elements are all there: isolation, a hidden, poorly understood danger lurking in the shadows, victims picked off one by one. Of course, that is figurative, but Amityville in Space shows why filmmakers should never make things too literal. Amityville in Space is bad. Not so bad that it is good. So bad, it is bad. Your opinion on Amityville as a franchise likely depends on your tolerance for utter hogwash. The first movie, The Amityville Horror, released in 1979, is an effective, often quite creepy horror. Since then, the loose Amityville Horror franchise spans nine core Amityville movies and between 50 and 90 low-budget independent additions to the franchise. Amityville in Space is definitely at the cheapest end of the low-budget spectrum, and as the name suggests, it takes 112 Ocean Avenue further than ever before, to the year 3015 and the edge of a distant black hole. Literally, the only thing worth watching in Amityville in Space is the hilarious opening that sees a failed exorcism attempt cause the Amityville house to literally blast off the surface of Earth like a rocket.d Unfortunately, Amityville in Space isn't a corny "so-bad it's good" movie. It's just frustratingly bad. Perhaps disappearing into a black hole is the fate Amityville deserved all along, though with the name being in the public domain, Amityville movies will just keep coming. At least I didn't have to watch Amityville Death Toilet (yes, that really exists). 0 Uber Jasons out of 5. Avoid like a demonic pig called Jodie 3. Leprechaun 4: In Space (1996) (Image credit: Trimark Pictures) Leprechaun 4 sees the franchise that launched the career of Jennifer Aniston blast its titular antagonist into space. The Leprechaun, played by the unparalleled Warwick Davis, makes the voyage to the final frontier with tongue planted firmly in cheek, and the results are bloody glorious. The film sees the Leprechaun's attempts to woo a space princess rudely interrupted by space marines and the minor inconvenience of being blown apart by a grenade. The Leprechaun then exacts his revenge on the spacecraft of the marines, an impressively realized set for a straight-to-video horror movie in the mid-90s. If you want some camp horror fun on Halloween, the sight of the Leprechaun emerging fully formed from the pants of a space marine is probably going to be unbeatable. Fans of British sitcoms will be equally delighted by the appearance of Guy Siner ('Allo 'Allo's Lt. Hubert Gruber) as Dr. Mittenhand. While the rest of the cast play the ludicrousness of a leprechaun rampaging through a spaceship offing space marines relatively straight, Davis and Siner don't just chew the scenery; they suck it in like thespian black holes. As Mittenhand says: "Thank you, Harold, I do the jokes!" Of course, there is plenty of ropey CGI, as is standard for a 90s genre movie, but there is a wonderful practical creature at the movie's conclusion that pays tribute to David Cronemburg's The Fly. Less Brundle-Fly, more Mitten-Spider. Plus a death that is pure Looney Tunes and a Kaiju-sized leprechaun. Take that, Uber Jason. 4.5 Uber Jasons out of 5. Thank your Lucky Charms 4. Hellraiser 4: Bloodline (1996) (Image credit: Miramax Films) Another horror franchise heading to space for its fourth installment, and this one also came out in 1996. Hellraiser 4: Bloodline marks a real downturn in the fortunes of Hellraiser, being the last in the series to receive a theatrical release and the last to benefit from input from creator and horror maestro Clive Barker. The film has a portmanteau style beginning in 2127, as Dr. Paul Merchant attempts to solve the mystery of the Lament Configuration, then flashing back to its creation by Merchant's ancestor Phillip LeMarchand in France in 1796. The movie then jumps to 1996, when the Lament Configuration has inspired a skyscraper built by another of Merchant's ancestors. This second section also sees the franchise's figurehead Pinhead, played by Doug Bradley, come into conflict with the demonic Angelique. A conflict that is carried into 2127. Arguably, the CGI in Hellraiser: Bloodline is no better or worse than that of Leprechaun 4; the problem is the latter isn't taking itself seriously, but the former really is. You can't really expect a "fun" Hellraiser movie; that has never been their vibe, and they are better for the serious tone. But it means a poorly realized move to space really doesn't

item.title: Ebola outbreak not under control in Africa, CDC warns
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has warned that the Ebola outbreak spreading across parts of Africa remains uncontrolled, with more than 10,200 confirmed cases and over 5,000 deaths recorded across the continent. The Director-General of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, gave the warning on Friday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief programme, raising concerns about the continued transmission and changing geographical spread of the disease. Kaseya said the assessment followed a virtual ministerial meeting held on October 28, which brought together more than 42 ministers and over 600 participants, including representatives of international organisations and development partners, to review the outbreak and ongoing response efforts. “We analysed the data and we saw that the outbreak is not yet under control,” he said. He disclosed that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed infections, while the combined number of confirmed cases across the continent had exceeded 10,200. “We have achieved what is a number of 10,000 people confirmed cases in DRC and also, if we put together, it’s more than 10,200 confirmed cases across the continent,” Kaseya said. Kaseya said more than 5,000 people had died from the outbreak, although figures published by health authorities showed a slightly lower confirmed death toll. “We also saw that we have more than 5,000 people already passed on due to this outbreak,” he added. Kaseya also expressed concern over changes in the geographical spread of the disease, noting that its epicentre was shifting. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus and has affected several African countries, including the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria. The DRC remains the worst-affected country, accounting for the overwhelming majority of infections and deaths. Data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control showed that the country had recorded 10,193 confirmed cases and 4,960 related deaths as of October 28. Kenya has also reported nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, following an imported infection linked to the DRC. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20, after a 42-year-old Swiss woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja. The woman, who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, was isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers before being medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment after her condition stabilised. Her husband, who was identified as a close contact, was also evacuated. Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola cases. However, the WHO clarified that the development did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, explaining that health authorities were still monitoring people who had contact

The Director-General of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, gave the warning on Friday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief programme, raising concerns about the continued transmission and changing geographical spread of the disease. Kaseya said the assessment followed a virtual ministerial meeting held on October 28, which brought together more than 42 ministers and over 600 participants, including representatives of international organisations and development partners, to review the outbreak and ongoing response efforts. “We analysed the data and we saw that the outbreak is not yet under control,” he said. He disclosed that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed infections, while the combined number of confirmed cases across the continent had exceeded 10,200. “We have achieved what is a number of 10,000 people confirmed cases in DRC and also, if we put together, it’s more than 10,200 confirmed cases across the continent,” Kaseya said. Kaseya said more than 5,000 people had died from the outbreak, although figures published by health authorities showed a slightly lower confirmed death toll. “We also saw that we have more than 5,000 people already passed on due to this outbreak,” he added. Kaseya also expressed concern over changes in the geographical spread of the disease, noting that its epicentre was shifting. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus and has affected several African countries, including the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria. The DRC remains the worst-affected country, accounting for the overwhelming majority of infections and deaths. Data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control showed that the country had recorded 10,193 confirmed cases and 4,960 related deaths as of October 28. Kenya has also reported nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, following an imported infection linked to the DRC. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20, after a 42-year-old Swiss woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja. The woman, who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, was isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers before being medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment after her condition stabilised. Her husband, who was identified as a close contact, was also evacuated. Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola cases. However, the WHO clarified that the development did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, explaining that health authorities were still monitoring people who had contact with the patient. The organisation said Nigeria must complete the required 42-day monitoring period before an official Ebola-free declaration could be made. In its October 29 situation report, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) said 62 contacts linked to the index case had been identified and were being monitored. The agency added that no new contacts or symptomatic contacts had been identified in the preceding 24 hours. The continued spread of the disease has heightened concerns about cross-border transmission and the capacity of African countries to contain infectious diseases amid increased movement of people across the continent. item.title: How to open the Crimson Manor in Phantom Blade Zero
item.description: The Crimson Manor is a mysterious location in Phantom Blade Zero that you discover after riding a suspicious elevator in the Weeping Creek Valley . Although you can visit it in the first few hours of the game, the doors to the somber building won't budge until you have a unique key that fits the puppet-shaped lock. Unlocking the manor is a secondary mission, but one that helps you learn more about a central character and achieve the game's true ending.

item.title: 'Five churches set on fire by Muslims?' Fake news by Islamophobic social media accounts
item.description: Several social media accounts associated with sharing anti-immigrant views claim French Muslims were responsible for burning five churches on October 17 – the day the nation was rocked by en masse protests. But both this number and story are fictitious. The French government agency that monitors religious heritage sites confirmed only one fire in a church occured in recent days; its cause unknown.

item.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
item.description: Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one. A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It's very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says. A filtered collection “We don't fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth," Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars' gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.” Read full article Comments

item.title: MAGA: Why Trump's movement is fracturing?
item.description: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters. Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way. Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms? 🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
item.content:encoded: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters. Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way. Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms? 🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.
