item.title: NASA ends Swift space telescope mission after failed rescue attempt
item.description: null NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift space telescope, after a private satellite failed in its bold bid to rescue the aging spacecraft. That rescue mission was led by the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies, whose LINK spacecraft tried to meet up with Swift this summer to boost its orbit. That didn't work out, however, so Swift continues its fall back toward Earth. The telescope is expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere "in the next few weeks," NASA said in a statement on Friday (Oct. 23). That statement served primarily to announce the end of the Swift mission after more than 20 very productive years. The telescope launched to Earth orbit in November 2004, tasked with studying gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) — the most powerful explosions in the cosmos. Swift was designed to operate for two years, but it continued studying the high-energy universe for more than two decades. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington, said in the statement. NASA had hoped to keep Swift going even longer. In September 2025, the agency awarded a contract to the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies to rescue the observatory, which was falling back to Earth thanks to atmospheric drag. Swift has no thrusters capable of counteracting this drag. item.dc:creator: Mike Wall
item.content:encoded: null NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift space telescope, after a private satellite failed in its bold bid to rescue the aging spacecraft. That rescue mission was led by the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies, whose LINK spacecraft tried to meet up with Swift this summer to boost its orbit. That didn't work out, however, so Swift continues its fall back toward Earth. The telescope is expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere "in the next few weeks," NASA said in a statement on Friday (Oct. 23). That statement served primarily to announce the end of the Swift mission after more than 20 very productive years. The telescope launched to Earth orbit in November 2004, tasked with studying gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) — the most powerful explosions in the cosmos. Swift was designed to operate for two years, but it continued studying the high-energy universe for more than two decades. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington, said in the statement. NASA had hoped to keep Swift going even longer. In September 2025, the agency awarded a contract to the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies to rescue the observatory, which was falling back to Earth thanks to atmospheric drag. Swift has no thrusters capable of counteracting this drag. So Katalyst built a refrigerator-sized spacecraft called LINK, which aimed to rendezvous with Swift, grapple it with three robotic arms and boost it to a higher orbit, allowing the observatory to continue its science work. NASA and Katalyst stressed from the start that success was far from guaranteed. After all, LINK's mission was unprecedented: No private spacecraft had ever captured and boosted a satellite that wasn't designed to be serviced in this way. And the rate of Swift's orbital decay demanded a rapid timeline: LINK launched on July 3 , a little over nine months after Katalyst won the $30 million NASA Swift-rescue contract. LINK was not able to execute its very challenging mission. About three weeks after liftoff, it suffered problems with its propulsion system and orientation-maintaining reaction wheels, which caused it to start spinning at an unexpected rate . These issues prevented LINK from capturing and boosting Swift, but the private craft did manage to get within 7.5 to 9.3 miles (12 to 15 kilometers) of the observatory and photograph it. "From the beginning, this was a high-risk, high-reward mission," Domagal-Goldman said in a statement on Sept. 25 , the day that LINK fell back to Earth. "And while we'll be sad to see Swift's mission come to a close, we knew this boost effort would be worthwhile either way — advancing U.S. spacecraft servicing technology, challenging us to meet unprecedented mission timelines, and testing how we operate satellites to extend their time in low Earth orbit ," he added. Katalyst Space’s LINK robotic servicing spacecraft captured this view of one of its solar panels in Earth orbit in August 2026. (Image credit: Katalyst Space)) Swift — which was officially renamed the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in 2018, after its first principal investigator, who died a year earlier — gathered its last scientific data on Oct. 20, according to NASA's Friday update. During its long and storied career, the space telescope observed more than 2,000 GRBs. And it did other work, too, studying more than 1,400 supernova explosions, as well as eyeing asteroids, comets and black holes and conducting an all-sky survey in X-ray light. The mission's data has contributed to about 7,000 published scientific papers to date, according to NASA officials. And that number is sure to keep rising far into the future. "Swift leaves us with an extraordinary archive of multiwavelength observations that will fuel new discoveries for decades more," Domagal-Goldman said in the Oct. 23 statement.

item.title: 'Donnie Darko' at 25: How a giant rabbit, time loops, and teen angst became a sci-fi cult classic
item.description: null "Have you ever seen a portal?" The term "cult classic" has been loosely bandied about in cinematic circles until its definition has diluted into nothingness, but never has it been more appropriately applied than to director Richard Kelly’s strange psychological sci-fi thriller, "Donnie Darko", which celebrates its milestone 25th birthday today. Starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Drew Barrymore, Mary McDonnell, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Patrick Swayze, Jena Malone, and Noah Wyle, "Donnie Darko" was released on Oct. 26, 2001, into an unstable world still shocked by the catastrophic Sept. 11 terrorist attacks less than two months earlier. The thrust of the narrative revolves around an alternative universe accidentally forming via a supernatural anomaly after a jet engine falls off a commercial airliner and crashes through the roof of a suburban Virginia home, landing in the bedroom of our troubled title character. As the frightening phantom of Frank the Bunny warns, this parallel reality has a ticking clock that’ll result in its imminent collapse in just 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, and 12 seconds. From the haunting voice telling our heroic teen, "Wake up, Donnie," as the grandfather clock in the Darko residence ominously chimed midnight, to its exploration of the nature of mental illness, time travel paradoxes, fraudulent motivational speakers, teenage angst in the 1980s, and the logistics of interdimensional portals, "Donnie Darko" became an ideal parable for turbulent times. But Kelly's post-modern sci-fi fantasy emerged on the big screen when there existed a pervading fear of gathering in large groups as America was just beginning to recover and process the atrocities committed on 9/11. Newmarket Films was perplexed on precisely how to market the movie, as it is such a unique combination of genres that forges something far greater than the sum of its parts. Throughout that entire fall, "Donnie Darko" came and went in multiplexes with barely a whisper, pulling in just over $500K off of a meager $4.5 million budget. Years later, it would become a bona fide word-of-mouth sensation via several re-releases, home video editions, and further experiences in regularly sold-out midnight screenings on its way to earning cult status. "Donnie Darko" celebrates its 25th anniversary on Oct. 26, 2026. (Image credit: Newmarket Films) It's a deeply personal film that will affect any viewer who allows its meticulously slow build to seduce them into its dreamlike sphere. Much has been debated and discussed about its many metaphors and symbolism, which employed elements of a splintered universe long before the multiverse was hijacked by Hollywood superhero spectacles. It’s a raw meditation on death more than anything, and its labyrinth of quantum entanglements feeds our existential core. item.content:encoded: null "Have you ever seen a portal?" The term "cult classic" has been loosely bandied about in cinematic circles until its definition has diluted into nothingness, but never has it been more appropriately applied than to director Richard Kelly’s strange psychological sci-fi thriller, "Donnie Darko", which celebrates its milestone 25th birthday today. Starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Drew Barrymore, Mary McDonnell, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Patrick Swayze, Jena Malone, and Noah Wyle, "Donnie Darko" was released on Oct. 26, 2001, into an unstable world still shocked by the catastrophic Sept. 11 terrorist attacks less than two months earlier. The thrust of the narrative revolves around an alternative universe accidentally forming via a supernatural anomaly after a jet engine falls off a commercial airliner and crashes through the roof of a suburban Virginia home, landing in the bedroom of our troubled title character. As the frightening phantom of Frank the Bunny warns, this parallel reality has a ticking clock that’ll result in its imminent collapse in just 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, and 12 seconds. From the haunting voice telling our heroic teen, "Wake up, Donnie," as the grandfather clock in the Darko residence ominously chimed midnight, to its exploration of the nature of mental illness, time travel paradoxes, fraudulent motivational speakers, teenage angst in the 1980s, and the logistics of interdimensional portals, "Donnie Darko" became an ideal parable for turbulent times. But Kelly's post-modern sci-fi fantasy emerged on the big screen when there existed a pervading fear of gathering in large groups as America was just beginning to recover and process the atrocities committed on 9/11. Newmarket Films was perplexed on precisely how to market the movie, as it is such a unique combination of genres that forges something far greater than the sum of its parts. Throughout that entire fall, "Donnie Darko" came and went in multiplexes with barely a whisper, pulling in just over $500K off of a meager $4.5 million budget. Years later, it would become a bona fide word-of-mouth sensation via several re-releases, home video editions, and further experiences in regularly sold-out midnight screenings on its way to earning cult status. "Donnie Darko" celebrates its 25th anniversary on Oct. 26, 2026. (Image credit: Newmarket Films) It's a deeply personal film that will affect any viewer who allows its meticulously slow build to seduce them into its dreamlike sphere. Much has been debated and discussed about its many metaphors and symbolism, which employed elements of a splintered universe long before the multiverse was hijacked by Hollywood superhero spectacles. It’s a raw meditation on death more than anything, and its labyrinth of quantum entanglements feeds our existential core. "I remember pulling over to the side of the road to finish reading Richard's script and being mesmerized," Gyllenhaal told The Guardian . "It was clearly influenced by classic directors—Ron Howard, Steven Spielberg—but with this strange psychosis. It beautifully captured the experience of moving into adulthood: the world that felt so solid becoming movable and liquid. I thought, “This is what my adolescence felt like,” although I don’t speak, and have never spoken to, rabbits." Kelly was just 23 years old when he penned the "Donnie Darko" screenplay in only 28 days based on his own adolescence growing up in Virginia during the ‘80s. Coincidentally, that is the exact number of days Frank the Bunny declares will mark the end of the world, and it is also the same amount of time taken to complete the Southern California production shoot in 2000. Layered with ‘80s pop anthems like Echo & the Bunnymen's "The Killing Moon," Tears for Fears' "Head Over Heels," The Church's "Under the Milky Way," and Gary Jules' melancholy cover of Tears for Fears' "Mad World," Kelly's mysterious coming-of-age masterpiece still offers up a lucid nightmare tinged with a touch of consuming dread that lingers long after any screening. Kelly did release a director's cut in 2004 that adds extra footage and alters the soundtrack, but we recommend the original theatrical cut for the purist’s version of this classic! Considering today’s political strife, climate change concerns, AI paranoia, pharmaceutical overlords, and alienated youth culture, "Donnie Darko" and its 1988 election year setting still seems to have its finger on the zeitgeist's pulse, continuing to present provocative questions. This Halloween, check out "Donnie Darko's" mind-warping weirdness on this 25th anniversary occasion and let no one ever question your commitment to Sparkle Motion ever again!

item.title: Stuck for a Halloween outfit? Set phasers to stunning with the best Star Trek costumes
item.description: Are you a Star Trek fan about to beam down to a Halloween party? Maybe you want to give Trick or Treat a Trekkie twist? We've got you covered with costumes based on the iconic sci-fi franchise, from the original series through to Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Discovery and beyond. Adult costumes aside, we've also included outfits for younger Star Trek fans and props to round out your outfit. You needn't put them away when Halloween is over, either. Star Trek costumes are so universally recognized you can use them for cosplay purposes too, or the next time someone throws a Trek-themed party. Or, if you're not a fan of Star Trek, check out our round-up of the best space and sci-fi themed Halloween costumes . item.title: Olamide, Yemi Alade, Gyakie & More: 5 New Music Videos to Watch
item.description: Yemi Alade wearing a black-and-gold embroidered abaya paired with ornate gold hand jewellery in her ‘Alhaja’ music video, directed by Clarence Peters. Photo Credit: Yemi Alade/Instagram New music videos are giving us plenty of reasons to stay glued to our screens this week. Victony is serving up a COLORS performance, Olamide is taking us back to the streets, Yemi Alade is celebrating a woman who knows her worth, and Ghana’s Gyakie and King Promise are setting the mood for romance. From Lagos street scenes to smooth highlife rhythms, these five new visuals show just how much variety the music scene has to offer right now. So, grab your headphones, turn up the volume and get comfortable. These are five new music videos to add to your watchlist this week. Victony — ‘2FRESH’ (A COLORS SHOW) Nigerian artist Victony brings his signature charisma to the iconic COLORS stage with the performance video for ‘2FRESH’, a standout track from his album STARLIFE . The playful anthem centres on high fashion, lavish lifestyle, and irresistible attraction, with Victony using witty wordplay and references to luxury brands to celebrate a woman’s immaculate drip. Set against the signature monochromatic COLORS backdrop, the minimalist visual strips away distractions to highlight his magnetic vocal delivery, smooth melodic shifts, and effortless style. Yemi Alade — ‘Alhaja’ Mama Africa Yemi Alade delivers pure visual radiance with the official music video for ‘Alhaja’. Moving away from traditional romance, the track is a vibrant anthem of self-assurance, luxury, and female independence, exploring the confidence of a woman who knows her worth and commands every room she enters. The video captures her signature high-energy choreography, rich African aesthetics, and striking fashion pieces, translating the song’s empowering message into a lively visual feast. Olamide — ‘Burukutu’ Indigenous rap icon Olamide keeps the street-pop momentum going with the official music video for ‘Burukutu’. Named after the traditional indigenous brew, the track is an unapologetic celebration of resilience, unyielding street pride, and enjoying life on your own terms while tuning out critics. The visual brings this energy to life through gritty Lagos street scenes, vibrant night-party culture, and infectious group choreography that grounds the YBNL frontman firmly in his indigenous roots. Gyakie — ‘Your Body (Crazy)’ Adding a smooth, seductive tone to this week’s lineup, Ghanaian sensation Gyakie enchants with the visual accompaniment for ‘Your Body (Crazy)’. The song dives into the intense chemistry, thrill, and irresistible physical attraction of a blossoming romance. Blending English with Ghanaian phrasing, the cinematic video uses warm, moody lighting, intimate camera angles, and breezy styling to complement her honey-toned R&B vocals, creating a captivating visual experience. item.title: Record breaker! Astronomers spot powerful cosmic explosion that lasted 27 days
item.description: null Astronomers have spotted a remarkable gamma-ray burst (GRB) that's a real Incredible Hulk compared to other cosmic explosions of the same type. What makes this GRB so special is the fact that the central engine powering it remained active for around 27 days, flaring in X-rays following the initial blast. That's 20 days longer than the longest previous GRB on record. This record-breaking burst — which is designated GRB 220706A and was spotted on July 6, 2022 — is even more exciting because scientists don't know what the central engine powering it actually is. "In a nutshell, GRB 220706A is an extremely late X-ray flare. X-ray flaring is common following GRBs, but previously it has always come within the first few days after we detect the burst," study team member Benjamin Gompertz, of the University of Birmingham in England, told Space.com. "The fact that we see flaring at around 27 days in the GRB’s rest frame tells us that there’s an ongoing active process, and that’s unprecedented in the known population," Gompertz added. "The previous record for delayed flaring was about six days after the GRB." What created the Incredible Hulk of gamma-ray bursts? GRBs are some of the most powerful explosions in the cosmos. They have been linked to the collapse of a massive star, which also triggers a supernova and creates a black hole . This results in a long-duration GRB, while short-duration GRBs are thought to be triggered when two stellar remnants called neutron stars collide. GRB 220706A is an example of an ultra-long GRB, a rare cosmic blast of gamma rays in which the engine powering the GRB stays active for longer. They are incredibly rare, with their cause still unknown. "We don’t know what the central engine driving this outburst is, and that’s what makes this such a compelling event," Gompertz said. "The fact that we see a supernova tells us that a star has collapsed, which is the standard power source for GRBs, but it doesn’t immediately account for the extremely late flaring or unusually bright supernova. We can interpret that through previous events to some degree." Gompertz added that another ultra-long GRB detected in 2011, GRB 111209A , was associated with an unusually bright supernova (SN2011k) that had clear evidence for a central engine. The team behind that research determined that GRB 111209A is powered by a magnetar, a neutron star with a particular powerful magnetic field. In this case, the magnetic field is rotating at around 1,000 times per second. "Our supernova looks a lot like that one, so a magnetar might be present here. That ties in nicely with super-luminous supernovas, which are also thought to be magnetar-driven," Gompertz said. "Another possibility could be that the GRB jet and the supernova are colliding with shells of dense material that were ejected towards the end of the parent star’s life, as it became unstable and began ejecting its outer layers. This sort of event is also seen in the super-luminous supernova pop

item.content:encoded: null Astronomers have spotted a remarkable gamma-ray burst (GRB) that's a real Incredible Hulk compared to other cosmic explosions of the same type. What makes this GRB so special is the fact that the central engine powering it remained active for around 27 days, flaring in X-rays following the initial blast. That's 20 days longer than the longest previous GRB on record. This record-breaking burst — which is designated GRB 220706A and was spotted on July 6, 2022 — is even more exciting because scientists don't know what the central engine powering it actually is. "In a nutshell, GRB 220706A is an extremely late X-ray flare. X-ray flaring is common following GRBs, but previously it has always come within the first few days after we detect the burst," study team member Benjamin Gompertz, of the University of Birmingham in England, told Space.com. "The fact that we see flaring at around 27 days in the GRB’s rest frame tells us that there’s an ongoing active process, and that’s unprecedented in the known population," Gompertz added. "The previous record for delayed flaring was about six days after the GRB." What created the Incredible Hulk of gamma-ray bursts? GRBs are some of the most powerful explosions in the cosmos. They have been linked to the collapse of a massive star, which also triggers a supernova and creates a black hole . This results in a long-duration GRB, while short-duration GRBs are thought to be triggered when two stellar remnants called neutron stars collide. GRB 220706A is an example of an ultra-long GRB, a rare cosmic blast of gamma rays in which the engine powering the GRB stays active for longer. They are incredibly rare, with their cause still unknown. "We don’t know what the central engine driving this outburst is, and that’s what makes this such a compelling event," Gompertz said. "The fact that we see a supernova tells us that a star has collapsed, which is the standard power source for GRBs, but it doesn’t immediately account for the extremely late flaring or unusually bright supernova. We can interpret that through previous events to some degree." Gompertz added that another ultra-long GRB detected in 2011, GRB 111209A , was associated with an unusually bright supernova (SN2011k) that had clear evidence for a central engine. The team behind that research determined that GRB 111209A is powered by a magnetar, a neutron star with a particular powerful magnetic field. In this case, the magnetic field is rotating at around 1,000 times per second. "Our supernova looks a lot like that one, so a magnetar might be present here. That ties in nicely with super-luminous supernovas, which are also thought to be magnetar-driven," Gompertz said. "Another possibility could be that the GRB jet and the supernova are colliding with shells of dense material that were ejected towards the end of the parent star’s life, as it became unstable and began ejecting its outer layers. This sort of event is also seen in the super-luminous supernova population." An illustration showing a magnetar surrounded by green magnetic field lines at the heart of supernova wreckage (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) The team isn't quite sure how the central engine of this ultra-long GRB differs from that of others and why that resulted in 27 days of flaring. "One possibility is that it’s a much bigger star than we usually see producing GRBs," Gompertz said. "A bigger star would take longer to fall in on itself and so provide a longer-lived source of energy to power the jet." GRB sources may be members of a stellar population of massive, compact stars called Wolf-Rayet stars . These are 10 times wider that the sun, with around 10 times the mass of our star. However, even the collapse of such a star can't explain GRB 220706A. "To power GRB 220706A, we estimated we need a star more like 1,000 times the radius of the sun, which would require a population of stars known as blue supergiants," Gompertz said . "On the other hand, it may be the remnant that’s different. If this star produced a magnetar, it may be that 'normal' GRBs just collapse to black holes." The team thinks that the big question with GRBs like this one is whether they are members of the normal GRB population or a different kind of event. Having this second event, in addition to GRB 111209A, with an unusually bright supernova potentially adds weight to the idea that these are different stars. But the problem is not yet solved. "The incredibly late flares also strain our models for how jets are powered," Gompertz said. "It will be fascinating to see how future theoretical work can incorporate a power source from a collapsing star that can last for a month!" A core collapse supernova births a black hole and launches a GRB (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) There could be even longer-lasting GRBs out in the cosmos that we have thus far failed to detect. Gompertz explained why such detections are tricky. "GRBs this long are hard to detect because most of the satellites we use to find them are in low Earth orbit , which means the target is periodically blocked every 90 minutes or so," he explained. "That's fine for your typical 10- to 100-second-long GRB but becomes a nuisance when tracking much longer events. Long-lasting GRBs also seem to be more active in the X-rays rather than the gamma rays." The University of Birmingham researcher added that newly launched missions like the Einstein Probe , which is more sensitive in X-rays than gamma rays, may be the perfect instruments to find more ultra-long GRBs. "With any luck, we’ll get a few more of these to chase so that we can start trying to understand the incredible power sources that drive them," Gompertz concluded. A pre-peer-reviewed version of the team's research is featured on the repository site arXiv.

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe
item.content:encoded: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

Cooking with GameChangers is a business-reality and cooking competition show where business executives are filmed through a day in their life and thereafter engage in a cook-off to make the best meal, which would be tasted by the show judges, and an “Ultimate GameChanger” is announced. Season 1 of the show aired in 2024 and garnered over 60 million TV viewers in a quarter. Season 2 of Cooking with GameChangers premiered with a week-long cook-off that saw corporate leaders and media icons trade their laptops and workspaces for aprons and kitchen workstations in a dramatic twist. The cook-off week hosted by social media sensation, Steve Chuks , reached a crescendo on Friday, October 23rd, 2026, with a live-streamed event that featured an entertaining cook-off between the show host, Daniel Etim Effiong , and one of the show judges, M.I Abaga . People that followed live updates on Instagram @cookingwithgamechangers got to experience the unforgettable moments delivered all through the daily live cook-offs between industry giants. The live cook-offs can be watched here . The live cook-off spotlighted organisations that lead in their respective sectors, hence serving as a pat-on-the-back for the great work being done to stay at the top. This cook-off, however, pushed our corporate contestants to their limit as they battled against the ticking clock to present their best interpretation of the assigned dish of yam and egg with peppered sauce. The panel of judges also brought their unique perspectives from business, entertainment, food, culture and leadership, holding back nothing as they tasted, critiqued and delivered sharp, witty feedback before the winner got announced. The show’s executive producer, Seyi Banigbe , joined the panel of judges from Monday to Wednesday as she kept the contestants on their feet even as she bridged humour with her culinary grit while delivering a detailed analysis of each contestant’s cooking effort. Day 1 kicked off on Monday, 19th October, with a cook-off between companies leading in the ethnic radio broadcast industry. The battle was between Wazobia FM, represented by Ogar Justina , and Naija FM, represented by Godwin Aruwayo . item.title: Family Business Summit 2026: Calls for Stronger Succession Planning and Governance to Secure Generational Legacy
item.description: The Family Business Summit 2026 has concluded in Lagos with a call for Nigerian family businesses to strengthen governance, embrace succession planning and invest in next-generation leadership to build enterprises that endure beyond their founders. Held from October 15 to 17 under the theme “ Beyond the Founder: Scaling Family Businesses Across Generations ,” the summit convened business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, wealth management experts and family enterprise advisers for three days of discussions on business continuity, wealth preservation and sustainable growth. Organised by My Family, My Business, in partnership with BusinessDay and PwC , the summit featured keynote addresses, panel sessions, masterclasses, a Deal Room, a succession workshop and the Family Business Leadership Awards 2026 as discussions explored succession planning, family governance, investment strategies, global wealth structuring, women’s leadership, technology and international expansion. In his welcome address, Oghenevwoke Ighure, Convener of the summit, emphasised the need for family businesses to move beyond founder-dependent structures and establish institutions capable of surviving across generations. “ The success of this year’s summit reinforces our belief that family businesses need more than the determination of their founders to endure; they need the right structures, values and leadership to thrive across generations. Our goal is to create a platform where families can have honest conversations, learn from one another’s experiences and access the knowledge and networks required to build sustainable institutions. Ultimately, succession is not just about transferring ownership; it is about preparing the next generation to lead, preserve the family legacy and create even greater value for the future .” Frank Aigbogun , Publisher of BusinessDay, Sam Abu , Country Senior Partner, PwC Nigeria and Regional Senior Partner, West Market, and Bolaji Balogun, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chapel Hill Denham delivered keynote addresses, while Esiri Agbeyi , PwC Nigeria Partner and Africa Family Business Leader, presented findings from the PwC Africa Family Business Survey. Bolaji Balogun , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chapel Hill Denham, addressed the role of patient capital in building businesses that endure. “ Building a family business that endures across generations requires more than reinvesting capital; it demands a clear distinction between family wealth and corporate resources, strong governance, integrity and a relentless commitment to excellence ,” Balogun said, stressing the importance of capital markets, long-term financing and developing the competence and character of future generations. item.content:encoded: The Family Business Summit 2026 has concluded in Lagos with a call for Nigerian family businesses to strengthen governance, embrace succession planning and invest in next-generation leadership to build enterprises that endure beyond their founders. Held from October 15 to 17 under the theme “ Beyond the Founder: Scaling Family Businesses Across Generations ,” the summit convened business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, wealth management experts and family enterprise advisers for three days of discussions on business continuity, wealth preservation and sustainable growth. Organised by My Family, My Business, in partnership with BusinessDay and PwC , the summit featured keynote addresses, panel sessions, masterclasses, a Deal Room, a succession workshop and the Family Business Leadership Awards 2026 as discussions explored succession planning, family governance, investment strategies, global wealth structuring, women’s leadership, technology and international expansion. In his welcome address, Oghenevwoke Ighure, Convener of the summit, emphasised the need for family businesses to move beyond founder-dependent structures and establish institutions capable of surviving across generations. “ The success of this year’s summit reinforces our belief that family businesses need more than the determination of their founders to endure; they need the right structures, values and leadership to thrive across generations. Our goal is to create a platform where families can have honest conversations, learn from one another’s experiences and access the knowledge and networks required to build sustainable institutions. Ultimately, succession is not just about transferring ownership; it is about preparing the next generation to lead, preserve the family legacy and create even greater value for the future .” Frank Aigbogun , Publisher of BusinessDay, Sam Abu , Country Senior Partner, PwC Nigeria and Regional Senior Partner, West Market, and Bolaji Balogun, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chapel Hill Denham delivered keynote addresses, while Esiri Agbeyi , PwC Nigeria Partner and Africa Family Business Leader, presented findings from the PwC Africa Family Business Survey. Bolaji Balogun , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chapel Hill Denham, addressed the role of patient capital in building businesses that endure. “ Building a family business that endures across generations requires more than reinvesting capital; it demands a clear distinction between family wealth and corporate resources, strong governance, integrity and a relentless commitment to excellence ,” Balogun said, stressing the importance of capital markets, long-term financing and developing the competence and character of future generations. Sam Abu , Country Senior Partner, PwC Nigeria speaking on the importance of succession planning in family businesses, said: “ Inheritance is not the same as succession. While inheritance answers the question of ownership, succession goes much further to address who leads the business, how decisions are made, and the principles that guide those decisions. Building a family enterprise that thrives across generations requires deliberate structures and traditions that enable the business to evolve and transition successfully from one generation to the next, without remaining dependent on its founder .” The summit featured contributions from prominent business leaders and international experts, including Deola Sagoe of The House of Deola, Tomi Otudeko of Honeywell Group, Cosmas Maduka Jnr . of Coscharis Group, Tara Fela-Durotoye , Professor Jeremy Cheung of CUHK Business School and Lansberg Gersick Advisors, and Professor Dominique Turpin of CEIBS Europe. Other contributors included Charity Maduka-McFoy of Coscharis Group, Nene Bejide Founder Blanche Aigle Communications, Foluke Oyeleye of Honeywell Group, Kemi Ojenike of Meristem Family Office, Idowu Thompson of FirstBank, Zipo Lai of Invest Hong Kong, and Claire Machin and Chad Phillips of Suntera Global. The Family Business Leadership Awards 2026 recognised individuals and enterprises for their contributions to family business leadership, succession, innovation and stewardship. The late Otunba Michael Olasubomi “ Subomi ” Balogun , CON, received the posthumous Lifetime Achievement in Family Business Leadership Award. Honeywell Group received the Generational Excellence in Family Business Award, while Aminu Nyako of Sebore Farms was named Emerging NextGen Family Business Leader. Quits Aviation Group FZE and Coleman Wires & Cables received the Succession Planning Excellence Award; Toyin Bakare of SAS Textiles and Deola Sagoe of The House of Deola received the Women in Family Business Leadership Award; and Remi and Yinka Morgan of Laterna Ventures were recognised in the Couples in Family Business category. The Anyaegbu Family of Chisco Group was named Entrepreneurial Family of the Year, Coscharis Group received the Emerging Technology Award, and Ambassador Nimi Akinkugbe received the Family Wealth Literacy & Stewardship Champion Award and Special Recognition Award. The summit concluded on October 17 with a NextGen Mixer at Ilashe Beach Resort, Lagos, bringing together emerging family business leaders to strengthen connections and reflect on the future of family enterprise. The summit was sponsored and supported by Suntera Global, Diya Fatimilehin & Co., Meristem Family Office, FirstBank, Jewellery Banc, HGL, SAS Textiles, Adenia, Capital Advisors, Mauritius Commercial Bank (MCB), Starzs, Bemil Security, Daily Need Group, Radix, Iron and The Glenlivet . Blanche Aigle Communications served as PR partner, Invest Hong Kong Family Office as strategic partner, CEIBS as academic partner, and PwC as knowledge partner. item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Sola Sobowale, Gideon Okeke and More Return for The Covenant Part 2 | Watch Trailer
item.description: The lead cast of ‘The Covenant Part 2’ featured on the official movie poster ahead of its release on Netflix and Kava TV. If you watched the first season of The Covenan t, you probably still have a few questions about that ending. Well, it looks like we’re finally getting some answers. The action-thriller is returning for Part 2, and with everything that happened in the first season, there’s a lot to unpack when the story picks up again. Following its run on Netflix, creator and executive producer Vincent Okonkwo is bringing the series back for another chapter, this time with South African filmmaker King Shaft directing. And there’s something else to look forward to: the cast is getting bigger, with familiar Nollywood faces joined by actors from South Africa. Remember Dagogo? He’s getting pulled even deeper into dangerous gang conflicts as the family struggles to hold on to its empire. Between old betrayals, grief, revenge and the fight for control, the problems they faced in Season 1 are far from over. And with new alliances forming, things could get even more complicated. Sola Sobowale returns as Stella in the official poster for VSL Media’s ‘The Covenant Part 2’, streaming on Netflix and Kava TV. Sola Sobowale returns as Stella, the family’s formidable matriarch, alongside Gideon Okeke , Uzee Usman , Bimbo Manuel , Segun Arinze , Ivie Okujaye and Tope Olowoniyan . South African actors Vuyo Dabula and Sibusiso Jill are also joining the cast, bringing new characters into a story already filled with family rivalries and dangerous loyalties. Now, for the date you’ll want to remember. The Covenant Part 2 premieres on Netflix across Africa on 6 November 2026, while viewers outside Africa will be able to watch on Kava TV. So, if you’ve been waiting to find out what happens after that Season 1 cliffhanger, there’s not much longer to go. Dagogo, Stella and the rest of the family have some unfinished business, and we’ll soon find out how it all plays out. item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: Beyond the Skyline: How Landmark Waterview Apartment Is Shaping a New Era of Premium Living in Lagos
item.description: With 200-plus live, work and play apartments, panoramic Atlantic views and an established business and leisure destination at its doorstep, Landmark Africa ‘s latest residential development, Landmark Waterview Apartments , is positioning itself as a compelling addition to Lagos’ premium property market. The main value proposition is “ convenience living ”. Lagos has no shortage of ambitious residential developments. Across Victoria Island, Ikoyi and the Lekki corridor, new towers continue to reshape the city’s skyline, competing for the attention of homeowners and investors. Yet, as the premium property market becomes increasingly competitive, the question for developers is no longer simply how high they can build but what lasting value they can offer beyond the apartment itself. For Landmark Africa, the answer lies in a business model it has spent nearly three decades developing. With Landmark Waterview Apartments, the company is bringing residential ownership into one of Lagos’ most established business, leisure, and lifestyle destinations, combining contemporary homes with the commercial activity, hospitality infrastructure, and recreational experiences that have become synonymous with the Landmark brand. The 20-storey development, situated within Landmark Lagos ecosystem in Victoria Island, has apartments overlooking the Atlantic coastline and Lagos skyline. Approximately 40% of the apartments have already been sold, reflecting early market interest in a project that seeks to offer more than conventional apartment ownership. From Commercial Real Estate to Destination Development Landmark Africa’s journey began in 1997 with serviced offices, long before the concept of integrated lifestyle destinations became a prominent feature of Nigeria’s real estate market. Over the years, the company expanded into commercial property, mixed-use developments featuring hospitality, tourism, entertainment, and leisure components, developing a portfolio that reflects an increasingly diversified approach to real estate. Its flagship Landmark Lagos destination became one of the most visible expressions of that strategy. By bringing together corporate offices, event facilities, restaurants, hospitality, retail, andrecreational attractions, the company helped establish a destination that attracted more than four million visitors annually at its peak. The significance of that achievement extends beyond visitor numbers. It demonstrated Landmark’s ability to create and sustain commercial activity by attracting businesses and consumers to a shared destination. Waterview represents an important next step in that evolution: introducing residential ownership into an environment that has already established its commercial and lifestyle appeal. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: With 200-plus live, work and play apartments, panoramic Atlantic views and an established business and leisure destination at its doorstep, Landmark Africa ‘s latest residential development, Landmark Waterview Apartments , is positioning itself as a compelling addition to Lagos’ premium property market. The main value proposition is “ convenience living ”. Lagos has no shortage of ambitious residential developments. Across Victoria Island, Ikoyi and the Lekki corridor, new towers continue to reshape the city’s skyline, competing for the attention of homeowners and investors. Yet, as the premium property market becomes increasingly competitive, the question for developers is no longer simply how high they can build but what lasting value they can offer beyond the apartment itself. For Landmark Africa, the answer lies in a business model it has spent nearly three decades developing. With Landmark Waterview Apartments, the company is bringing residential ownership into one of Lagos’ most established business, leisure, and lifestyle destinations, combining contemporary homes with the commercial activity, hospitality infrastructure, and recreational experiences that have become synonymous with the Landmark brand. The 20-storey development, situated within Landmark Lagos ecosystem in Victoria Island, has apartments overlooking the Atlantic coastline and Lagos skyline. Approximately 40% of the apartments have already been sold, reflecting early market interest in a project that seeks to offer more than conventional apartment ownership. From Commercial Real Estate to Destination Development Landmark Africa’s journey began in 1997 with serviced offices, long before the concept of integrated lifestyle destinations became a prominent feature of Nigeria’s real estate market. Over the years, the company expanded into commercial property, mixed-use developments featuring hospitality, tourism, entertainment, and leisure components, developing a portfolio that reflects an increasingly diversified approach to real estate. Its flagship Landmark Lagos destination became one of the most visible expressions of that strategy. By bringing together corporate offices, event facilities, restaurants, hospitality, retail, andrecreational attractions, the company helped establish a destination that attracted more than four million visitors annually at its peak. The significance of that achievement extends beyond visitor numbers. It demonstrated Landmark’s ability to create and sustain commercial activity by attracting businesses and consumers to a shared destination. Waterview represents an important next step in that evolution: introducing residential ownership into an environment that has already established its commercial and lifestyle appeal. For buyers, this means investing in a property connected to an existing destination rather than relying solely on the promise of future neighbourhood development. A Waterfront Address with a Distinctive Proposition A major attraction of Landmark Waterview Apartments is its position within Victoria Island, one of Lagos’ principal centres for business, hospitality and high-value residential property. The development offers city, mixed and ocean views, with selected corner apartments designed to provide expansive outlooks, additional natural light and generous living spaces. Its design also incorporates two dedicated leisure floors, with facilities including an infinity swimming pool, gym, spa, children’s recreational areas, games room and outdoor lounges. Smart-home technology, concierge services and controlled access are intended to support residents’ convenience and security. An important part of the wider development vision is the proposed artificial beachfront and canal experience, which would introduce a distinctive recreational feature to the residential offering. The ambition is to combine the appeal of coastal living with a broad range of private amenities and access to established leisure and hospitality facilities. This leisure integration is particularly relevant in Lagos, where proximity to business districts, recreational destinations, and essential services can significantly influence how residents experience the city. For professionals with demanding schedules, families seeking accessible recreational facilities and buyers who divide their time between Nigeria and other countries, these considerations can be as important as the residences themselves. The Investment Case: Owning a Home That Can Also Work as an Asset Landmark Waterview’s investment appeal extends beyond its architectural design and location. The development is being marketed to a diverse range of buyers, including Nigerian professionals, high-net-worth individuals, diaspora investors and corporate organisations seeking residential accommodation in Victoria Island. A buyer may acquire an apartment as a primary residence, maintain it as a home for visits to Lagos or explore opportunities within the long-term rental and short-let markets. For investors seeking a different ownership arrangement, the Landmark Executive Apartments model offers access to a professionally managed hospitality investment structure, subject to its applicable terms. This range of possibilities underpins the development’s proposition: Own it. Use it. Earn from it. The concept is particularly relevant to diaspora buyers, who may want to maintain a residential base in Nigeria without leaving the property entirely unused during extended periods abroad. Corporate buyers may also find value in apartments that can accommodate executives, expatriate employees or visiting personnel within an established commercial district. Although investment returns remain subject to market conditions, operating costs and occupancy performance, the opportunity to combine personal use with potential income generation broadens the property’s relevance beyond traditional homeownership. With apartments marketed from approximately US$125,000, subject to availability and pricing changes, Waterview offers several entry points into the development. From Market Interest to Delivery Beyond its commercial positioning, Landmark Waterview is entering an important phase in its development. The 20-storey project has reached its 13th floor, with construction progressing towards a targeted completion date in the fourth quarter of 2027. The current reported sale of approximately 40% of its apartments also provides an indication of buyer interest ahead of completion. For Landmark Africa, delivering Waterview represents an opportunity to strengthen its position within Lagos’ residential market while expanding an operating model historically associated with commercial property, hospitality and leisure. A New Chapter in Landmark’s Lagos Story Nearly three decades after Landmark Africa began operations, Waterview reflects how far the company’s development strategy has evolved. From serviced offices to major commercial and leisure destinations, its growth has been shaped by an ability to identify opportunities and develop properties that respond to changing patterns of business and consumer demand. Waterview carries that thinking into residential real estate, with a development that combines the appeal of an Atlantic-facing address, the Landmark ecosystem. Contemporary residential facilities, and investment flexibility. Its longer-term significance will be measured not only by the addition of 274 apartments to Lagos’ residential market, but by the value delivered to homeowners and investors as the development becomes operational. For Landmark Africa, it is another opportunity to demonstrate how its experience in business, hospitality, and leisure can be translated into a differentiated residential offering. For buyers, it presents the prospect of owning a home within a destination that has already become part of Lagos’ commercial and social landscape. Landmark Waterview Apartments — Your ho

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: BellaNaija’s Omotunde is Off to South Korea For LG Electronics Press Tour
item.description: Hey BNers! Guess who’s off to South Korea? Yours truly! I’m super excited to share that LG has invited us on a press tour to South Korea, and I honestly can’t wait to see what they have in store for us. From getting an inside look at some of LG’s innovations to visiting its facilities and flagship spaces, this promises to be an exciting opportunity to see a different side of the brand and experience some of the technology that goes into the products we use every day. Our itinerary will take us from Seoul to Busan, and while I’m looking forward to the LG experience, I’m also secretly hoping there’ll be enough time to explore a little beyond the official schedule. Because, let’s be honest, how does one travel all the way to South Korea and not try to soak in some of its beauty? And BNers, we need to talk about the K-drama dreams! If you know me, you know I’m already imagining the beautiful streets, cute cafés, familiar-looking locations, and all those little moments that make you feel like you’ve stepped right into an episode of your favourite Korean drama. Hopefully, I get a little time to wander around, discover some hidden gems, sample Korean food, and take in the culture. Who knows? I just might get to live out my K-drama princess dreams for a day or two. And before anyone asks, yes, I am fully prepared to be a little dramatic about it. If I find myself walking down a beautiful Seoul street with the perfect autumn backdrop, please allow me my main-character moment. If there’s a cute café that looks like it belongs in a romance drama, just know that I’m probably stopping for pictures. And if I happen to run into your favourite oppa while I’m out and about? Well, BNers, you’ll be the first to know! But beyond the K-drama fantasies, I’m genuinely looking forward to experiencing South Korea for myself, seeing its culture up close, discovering new places, and sharing the experience with you all. So, here’s where you come in! If you could send me anywhere in South Korea, where would it be? Is there a K-drama filming location you’ve always wanted to see? A Korean dish you think I absolutely must try? A café, shopping district, street, or attraction that deserves a spot on my itinerary? So, stay glued to BellaNaija because we’re taking this trip together. And who knows? You might just get to experience a little bit of South Korea through my eyes. Seoul, Busan, K-drama dreams, and LG adventures? I’m ready! Catch all the deets on the @bellanaija Instagram soon. Annyeonghaseyo, BNers! See you on the other side. The post BellaNaija’s Omotunde is Off to South Korea For LG Electronics Press Tour appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Lara Croft is 30! We look at the video game icon’s biggest blunders
item.description: We all know the highlights of the tomb raider’s storied career – but what about the lowlights? We dig deep to unearth the archaeologist’s less glorious moments Happy birthday, Lara! This month marks 30 years since Ms Croft first swan-dived into our lives with her unique blend of athletic prowess, archaeological expertise and giant knockers. More than 100 million Tomb Raider games have been sold since. We all remember the good times: the bold design and sheer playability of the original titles; the establishment of Lara as a 90s icon, embodying both lads’ mag culture and girl power; the way she made games cool, even appearing on the cover of the Face. We’ve had blockbuster movies, big budget reboots, and shiny reissues . And who could forget the time we got to powerwash her house ? But no one gets to 30 without a few skeletons in the closet – or in Lara’s case, butlers in the freezer. So here’s a look at the darker parts of her past. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Veekee James’ Sheer Beaded Bodice Leads Wine-Red Fashion at Zlatan Ibile’s Wedding | See Photos
item.description: Veekee James showcasing her custom wine-red corset dress and gold woven box clutch. Veekee James at a party? Trust her to come dressed like the celebration has its own red carpet. And when it’s a Nigerian wedding, with good music, beautiful traditional outfits and guests who take their fashion very seriously, you already know she’s going to have some fun with her look. Yesterday, Afrobeats star Zlatan Ibile , whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and his partner, Davita Omoniyi , celebrated their traditional wedding with family, friends and some familiar faces from the entertainment industry. Among the guests was Nigerian fashion designer Veekee James, who arrived in a gorgeous wine-red and champagne creation from her own fashion label. And between the sculpted corset, the beaded sleeves and that towering gele, there was so much to admire. Veekee James in a custom wine-red sheer corset dress with metallic sequin detailing and a structured metallic gele. Let’s start with the dress. Veekee chose a floor-length, figure-hugging design featuring a sheer corset-style bodice covered in vertical rows of wine-red crystals. The sweetheart-inspired neckline extended into a high, embellished collar, while the long sheer sleeves featured rows of burgundy beads. The fitted skirt followed a mermaid silhouette, with sweeping patterns of gold sequins, wine-red embroidery and dusty-rose detailing running down to a subtle train. Structural details of the sheer corset bodice, crystal neckband, and sequin wave skirt on Veekee James’ wedding guest dress. And that gele! Veekee went for a tall, fan-pleated design in metallic champagne, giving her look even more height and making the headwrap a fashion moment of its own. She paired it with burgundy drop earrings, a structured gold woven box clutch and soft, neutral makeup that complemented the colours of her outfit. Styling details of Veekee James’ high-neck crystal collar, sheer corset bodice, and pleated metallic gele. Of course, Veekee knows her way around a corset. As the founder and creative director of her eponymous fashion label, she’s known for sculpted silhouettes, detailed beadwork and glamorous occasionwear. For Zlatan and Davita’s wedding, she brought those design elements into her own wardrobe, pairing a fitted, heavily embellished dress with a traditional gele. What we particularly love is how the colours work together. The deep wine-red gives the dress its richness, while the champagne and gold details brighten the overall look. Even with the crystals, beading and high neckline, the accessories have their place, from the matching earrings to the gold clutch. Veekee James posing alongside her husband Femi Atere at Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s wedding. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Veekee James showcasing her custom wine-red corset dress and gold woven box clutch. Veekee James at a party? Trust her to come dressed like the celebration has its own red carpet. And when it’s a Nigerian wedding, with good music, beautiful traditional outfits and guests who take their fashion very seriously, you already know she’s going to have some fun with her look. Yesterday, Afrobeats star Zlatan Ibile , whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and his partner, Davita Omoniyi , celebrated their traditional wedding with family, friends and some familiar faces from the entertainment industry. Among the guests was Nigerian fashion designer Veekee James, who arrived in a gorgeous wine-red and champagne creation from her own fashion label. And between the sculpted corset, the beaded sleeves and that towering gele, there was so much to admire. Veekee James in a custom wine-red sheer corset dress with metallic sequin detailing and a structured metallic gele. Let’s start with the dress. Veekee chose a floor-length, figure-hugging design featuring a sheer corset-style bodice covered in vertical rows of wine-red crystals. The sweetheart-inspired neckline extended into a high, embellished collar, while the long sheer sleeves featured rows of burgundy beads. The fitted skirt followed a mermaid silhouette, with sweeping patterns of gold sequins, wine-red embroidery and dusty-rose detailing running down to a subtle train. Structural details of the sheer corset bodice, crystal neckband, and sequin wave skirt on Veekee James’ wedding guest dress. And that gele! Veekee went for a tall, fan-pleated design in metallic champagne, giving her look even more height and making the headwrap a fashion moment of its own. She paired it with burgundy drop earrings, a structured gold woven box clutch and soft, neutral makeup that complemented the colours of her outfit. Styling details of Veekee James’ high-neck crystal collar, sheer corset bodice, and pleated metallic gele. Of course, Veekee knows her way around a corset. As the founder and creative director of her eponymous fashion label, she’s known for sculpted silhouettes, detailed beadwork and glamorous occasionwear. For Zlatan and Davita’s wedding, she brought those design elements into her own wardrobe, pairing a fitted, heavily embellished dress with a traditional gele. What we particularly love is how the colours work together. The deep wine-red gives the dress its richness, while the champagne and gold details brighten the overall look. Even with the crystals, beading and high neckline, the accessories have their place, from the matching earrings to the gold clutch. Veekee James posing alongside her husband Femi Atere at Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s wedding. And if you’ve been looking for wedding guest inspiration, Veekee’s outfit offers a lovely styling idea: when your dress has this much detail around the neckline, you can leave out the necklace and let your earrings and gele do their thing. With her wine-red corset dress and metallic champagne headwrap, Veekee James gave us another beautiful take on Nigerian wedding guest fashion. Veekee James with her husband, Femi Atere, attending Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s traditional wedding ceremony. Femi wears an off-white Agbada set with embroidered front details and a matching Fila cap, while Veekee coordinates in a wine-red sheer corset dress and gold clutch bag. *** Photo Credit: Veekee James/Instagram The post Veekee James’ Sheer Beaded Bodice Leads Wine-Red Fashion at Zlatan Ibile’s Wedding | See Photos appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi celebrating their Yoruba cultural heritage during their wedding ceremony. Lemon yellow and mint green? Now that’s a colour combination we can get behind. For their second traditional wedding look, Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi ( Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael ) have switched things up, trading their earlier burgundy and ivory outfits for a softer palette that feels right at home at a Yoruba wedding. And if you thought one outfit change was enough for this celebration, you know Nigerian weddings better than that! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in custom Mazelle Bridal pastel Yoruba traditional attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. After honouring Davita’s Edo heritage in their first look, the couple are now celebrating Zlatan’s Yoruba roots in coordinated outfits by Mazelle Bridal. Davita wears a custom lemon-yellow gown with a sculpted, corset-style bodice, a sweetheart-inspired neckline and long sleeves with flared cuffs. Mint-green appliqué forms swirling, floral-inspired patterns across the bodice and fitted, floor-length skirt, with gold-toned accents adding extra detail. Davita Omoniyi showcasing her custom Mazelle Bridal outfit for her Yoruba traditional wedding look. She completes the look with a large, pleated lemon-yellow gele and matching sheer fabric draped over her arm. A green statement necklace, matching earrings and a mint-green clutch bring the accessories together, while the soft yellow and green palette gives her bridal look a fresh, coordinated finish. Davita Omoniyi wearing a pleated circular gele and sheer veil for her second traditional wedding outfit change. Zlatan matches her in a custom mint-green agbada by Mazelle Bridal, featuring subtle embroidery across the chest. He finishes his outfit with a structured fila, layers of white beads and a carved green walking stick that picks up the colour of his attire. Zlatan Ibile in a custom Mazelle Bridal Agbada set for his Yoruba traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple pose hand in hand against a plum backdrop. Their first look celebrated Davita’s Edo heritage, and this second outfit honours Zlatan’s Yoruba roots, giving their wedding wardrobe two lovely cultural chapters. And with lemon yellow and mint green taking centre stage, this outfit change has given us another reason to keep up with their wedding style. Davita Omoniyi and Zlatan Ibile posing together in matching pastel Mazelle Bridal attire. *** Photo Credit: Zlatan Ibile/Instagram The post Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: How AI Can Expand Opportunities for African Youth – Discussions to Expect at Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar
item.description: AI could be a great equaliser, but only if it’s built intentionally to benefit the people who need it most. Credit: Gates Foundation . During the 2026 ADF-YGL Convening in Lagos , young leaders from across the world, including Africa, gathered at Learn2Earn Academy, an AI talent factory founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji . There, the global leaders were introduced to a few students who have been using AI to build solutions for some of the day-to-day challenges that Africans, Nigerians specifically, face. One of them was Anas Masama, who showcased ‘Morrow’, a fintech app that allows offline transfers without internet connectivity. Anas explained that despite the wide coverage of internet providers in Nigeria, the internet’s strength fluctuates or sometimes goes offline and leaves Nigerians stranded at a point of payment. With AI, he built ‘Morrow’ to solve two problems: 1) The embarrassment that a Nigerian might feel due to bad internet connectivity. 2) Time. Anas’ invention is an example of the potential opportunities that exist when Africans leverage AI to solve basic issues. While there are concerns about the risks of AI use in Africa, including hallucinations, stereotypical results and many others, it remains one of the fastest-growing technological advancements in recent times. AI continues to grow and become more efficient, and the most urgent task Africans can embark on is to upskill in how to adopt AI for better use, so the continent doesn’t get left behind. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates calls for three actions now that will help AI improve lives and livelihoods for more people in the years ahead: Make AI tools work in every language people speak; ground AI tools in local data; and invest in people and access in the places and populations they are intended to serve. All three suggestions apply to Africa so it can properly leverage AI to expand opportunities. At present, despite how expansive AI has become, it is built in places far away from Africa. This is why Africans, who have access to local data and speak African languages, should build AI tools that incorporate local data and African languages for better use. This way, AI has access to specific data of Africans and will allow it to better understand cultural contexts and pragmatics. This will make a great equaliser rather than make things less equal. Of course, Africans still encounter basic challenges like electricity, connectivity, access to phones, and other issues, but those who have access must maximise it greatly to help others. This year’s Goalkeepers 2026 is centred around this conversation. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29. This event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth”, aims to discuss how AI can create opportunities for Africans across various sectors while also addressing the challenges the continent faces.
